story.fullStory:
Amy Winehouse's "Rehab" reached #9 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Rehab" is a song written and recorded by the English singer-songwriter Amy Winehouse, from her second and final studio album Back to Black (2006).

Produced by Mark Ronson, the lyrics are autobiographical and address Winehouse's refusal to enter a rehabilitation clinic for alcohol.

"Rehab" was released as the lead single from Back to Black in 2006, and it peaked at number 7 in the United Kingdom on its Singles Chart and number 9 in the United States on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming Winehouse's only top 10 hit in the US.

The song peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 20 weeks on the chart.
